title: Logic Drummer Tricks
intro: Drummer is not a loop library. It is a performance engine that responds to what the rest of your arrangement is doing, and once you know where the controls are it will out‑play most programmed parts.

tips.t: Use Complexity and Intensity, then the kit-piece controls
tips.d: The Drummer keeps its X/Y pad in 10.7, 11 and 12 — drag the puck right for a busier part, up for a louder one, and use the Complexity Range sliders to offset individual kit pieces against it. Logic 11 renamed the surrounding editor to the Session Player Editor and added Bass Player and Keyboard Player alongside the Drummer; Complexity and Intensity sliders are those two players' controls, not the Drummer's.

tips.t: Change the drummer, not just the preset
tips.d: Each drummer character has genuinely different playing tendencies. If a preset is close but the feel is wrong, swap the drummer rather than hunting for another preset — but click the lock next to any setting you want to survive the swap (the Fills knob has one), because Apple's locks exist precisely to 'prevent any changes to the setting when switching presets or drummers'.

tips.t: Turn individual kit pieces on and off per region
tips.d: Click a kit piece in the editor to enable or disable it for that region only. Drop the crash out of the verse and back in for the chorus.

tips.t: Convert a Drummer region to MIDI and edit it by hand
tips.d: Right‑click the region and choose Convert > Convert to MIDI Region. You get the full performance in the Piano Roll to nudge, delete and re‑velocity as you like.

tips.t: Use the Details panel for feel, ghost notes and hi‑hat
tips.d: Click the Details button in the Drummer Editor to reveal Feel (drag right to play ahead of the beat, left to play behind it), Ghost Notes (syncopated snare and kick hits), Hi-Hat openness and Humanize. This is where a stiff pattern becomes a groove.

tips.t: Swap the kit without losing the performance
tips.d: The Drummer track's instrument depends on the drummer: acoustic drummers load Drum Kit Designer, electronic and hip-hop drummers load Drum Machine Designer. Click the kit icon or kit name at the left of the editor to open whichever one is loaded. In Drum Kit Designer you can exchange the kit and, per selected piece, adjust Tune (pitch), Dampen (sustain) and Gain — and on multi-channel kits switch the Overheads mic in or out and pick room A, room B or no room emulation — all without touching a single note.
